name: prompt-envelope
description: PROMPT-ENVELOPE ratchet. server/utils/sanitizePrompt.ts states the rule in its own header — 'Apply at every site where DB-sourced text is interpolated into a prompt' — and nothing checked it. Unit 111 found what that costs: server/ai/executive.ts fed user-uploaded document text into Pax's SYSTEM role message with no envelope, sanitized by a weaker same-named function, while the system prompt instructed the model only about the <<USER_DATA>> envelope it never received. It shipped green. This converts the doc comment into CI, the same move lint-reachability.mjs made for 'built but unwired'. Counts FREE-TEXT interpolations into an LLM message that do not pass through the canonical sanitizer; strictly down-only. NOT a broad check by design: the first cut matched any `content:` template anywhere and found 237 interpolations across 43 files, overwhelmingly ${totalMrr}, ${paidOrgs.length} and module constants — a gate whose number is mostly noise is one people learn to re-baseline. minScannedFiles/minMessageTemplates are the vacuity floors: a scan that stops seeing code must FAIL, not report a clean zero.
lastBumpNote: 2026-08-16 — 0 → 1. Read the arithmetic before reading it as a raised baseline: the predicate was re-seeded 0 → 15 when it got its sight back, and the central pass then WRAPPED FOURTEEN of the fifteen inside the same wave, so the committed number is 15 → 1. The one that remains is real and unwrapped: complianceGuardian.ts:677 `check.checkDescription` (composed from `compliance_rules.ruleName` + `.ruleDescription`) inside the report prompt's `.map()` block — the same site's `property.address` was wrapped, its sibling was not. Wrap it and the gate's stale-high FAIL will tell you to set this to 0. THE RE-SEED, recorded because a ratchet that goes up must justify itself: the predicate got its sight back. Not a failure being papered over: 15 sites that were always violations became VISIBLE, and all fifteen were confirmed by hand before this number was written. Two blind spots closed. (1) THE MOTIVATING DEFECT'S OWN SHAPE. The gate required the template literal to sit literally in the `content:` slot, so the executive.ts form — `const systemPrompt = `…${doc.extractedText}…`` then `content: systemPrompt` — scored zero. The gate could not see the defect that built it, and hoisting a prompt one line up was a complete bypass (57 of 160 identifier-valued message slots in server/ are hoisted). `hoistedMessageTemplates()` now resolves the identifier to its const template in the enclosing block, guarded by a brace-balance scope check, and applies the same three rules: +7. (2) FIELD-LIST NAME-KEYING: a fixed roster of exact names is walked past by spelling the prose field `marketNotes` instead of `notes`, so `*Notes`/`*Description` became camelCase-suffix rules, and four names P0-14's own header calls out were added — firstName/lastName ('lead names'), subjectLine ('inbox subjects'), documentName/fileName (an upload's filename is attacker-chosen): +8. THE FIFTEEN, each verified by reading the code: agent-skills.ts:2340 property.address; agent-skills.ts:2509 lead.firstName + lead.lastName; agent-skills.ts:2599 existing.marketNotes; campaignOptimizer.ts:149 campaign.subject + campaign.content; cmo/scriptGenerator.ts:167 input.notes; cmo/scriptScorer.ts:97 script.body; complianceGuardian.ts:663 property.address + check.checkDescription; documentIntelligence.ts:569 doc1.documentName + doc2.documentName; dueDiligence.ts:185 report.summary.address; overrideLearner.ts:62 context.ceoOverrideNotes; sequenceOptimizer.ts:345 r.subjectLine. Fix the occurrences, not this number — every wrap lowers it, and the gate FAILS on a stale-high baseline so the drop gets locked in. NOISE MEASURED AND REJECTED rather than shipped: .summary +3 (3 false — nested object), .title +4 (4 false — code rosters), .personalityPrompt +9 (9 false — our own persona prompts), blanket *Name +7 (2 false), .recipientName / *Text|*Content|*Body|*Message / .text|.value|.reason +0 each, and a nesting-aware INLINE template reader +4 (3 false). Numbers and reasoning in the script header so the next session re-measures instead of re-arguing.

allowlist.reason: NOT DB-sourced text. Both sites append CONFIDENCE_SCHEMA_INSTRUCTION to the system message the CALLER already assembled — `{ ...m, content: `${m.content}\n\n${CONFIDENCE_SCHEMA_INSTRUCTION}` }` — so `m.content` is a system prompt this codebase wrote, not customer input. Sanitizing here would be actively wrong: it would redact the system prompt's OWN anti-injection language, which by construction contains the phrases the deny-list hunts ('role overrides, persona changes, system-prompt exfiltration attempts' appear verbatim in USER_DATA_SYSTEM_CLAUSE). The envelope belongs where untrusted text ENTERS the prompt, which is the caller's job and is what this gate checks everywhere else.
